content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 10.4 (p0185) makes M&I the owner of any work of authorship created for us "even if paid for by Customer" and lets M&I resell it to its other customers, with no licence back; §17.2 reinforces that we have "no rights" in M&I materials beyond use during the Term, and the Article 23 source-code licence is term-limited and non-sublicensable. That fails the IP fallback.

**Position taken:** fallback (M&I retains ownership of its programs and know-how — already met verbatim in 10.4), cured by two surgical edits:
1. New §10.5 granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for our business.
2. One added sentence in §17.1 limiting M&I's processing of Customer Data to providing the Services (the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" standard in 17.4 was too wide); our existing sole-ownership sentence in 17.1 was left untouched.

We did not attempt to reverse ownership to preferred level, since that would require collateral rewrites of §17.2 and Article 23.
